_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Ice Climber (USA, Europe, Korea) - ADR-0239,
PRD Part A slice F14.17. Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2. ADR-0239 s1 says to use the first rung that reaches
the place, and for Ice Climber that is rung 1: the game's own selector, by
input. navigation.kind is 'input', so no cheat rides with any session and
every session is an ADR-0184 s2 'clean' pass that all four surfaces may
read. Rung 2 is not used even though it IS available: Data Crystal's RAM
map for this game publishes 0x0059 'Level Number', which is the same
mountain index the title screen's selector writes, so a pinned 0059:VV
would warp the boot's own level load. Rung 1 is preferred because it is
the code the developers shipped (ADR-0184 s3 rank 1): the game fills its
own level variable through its own routine, nothing substitutes on the CPU
read bus, and every byte the session's final state holds is the game's own.
THE SELECTOR THE GAME OFFERS. The Ice Climber instruction booklet
(Nintendo of America, 1985; archive.org, item
'Ice-Climber-Manual-NES-US-1985', file
'Ice-Climber-Manual-NES-US-1985_djvu.txt'), 'Rules and Suggestions' 1:
'Use the control pad when the game menu is displayed to enter the number
of the mountain you want to climb. (MOUNTAIN XX)'
'The mountains are numbered from 1 ~ 32. You can attempt to climb any
mountain, but the larger the number the more difficult the mountain is
to climb.'
and its controller page: 'SELECT button - Move the hammer mark ( < ) to
the game you wish to select from the game menu by pressing this button.'
and 'START button - Press this button to begin.'
Read off this ROM's own screen (screenshots under
runs/f1417/iceclimber/probe/st-*, 2026-09-26) the title menu is three
rows - '1 PLAYER GAME', '2 PLAYER GAME', 'MOUNTAIN 01' - with the hammer
mark beside the first row. Two of the three agree with the booklet by
measurement: SELECT moves the hammer mark between the two player rows
(rows 128-151 and columns 57-63 of the frame change, nothing else), and
every d-pad direction redraws only the two digits of 'MOUNTAIN nn' (rows
160-166), so on this screen the d-pad is the mountain number and nothing
else. Measured on all four directions: Down and Right add one, Up and Left
subtract one, and the number wraps - Left from 01 reads 32, a 32nd Right
reads 01 again. $0059 (below) was read off the final state of every one of
those probes and tracks the displayed number exactly.
Both players' menus reach the same 32 mountains, so this sweep is the
1-player menu, which is the default the hammer mark starts on: a 2-player
session draws Nana as well and is a body a later measurement can name,
not a place the selector reaches that this one misses.
THE VALUES, AND WHICH MOUNTAIN IS NOT ONE. All 32 mountains are swept.
Thirty-one of them are values here - MOUNTAIN 02 through MOUNTAIN 32 - and
MOUNTAIN 01 is deliberately absent because it is what this sweep measures
AGAINST: ADR-0239 s5 names 'the game's current stage-1 route' as the before
side, and for a game with no route set the current route is what the power
switch produces - the title menu's own default, MOUNTAIN 01, pressed
through with START and nothing else. That route is recorded separately with
this profile's own defaults.entry and body
(runs/f1417/iceclimber/before/) and folded in with --baseline. A value for
MOUNTAIN 01 would be a byte-identical recording of the baseline and would
report new == 0, which ADR-0239 s4 reads as did-not-warp; the same trap
Ninja Gaiden's profile documented for its Act 1-1 and Excitebike's for
neither. So the sweep is 31 values, the union covers 32 mountains, and the
one mountain that is not a value is the one that defines the before column.
WHERE THE D-PAD PRESSES LIVE, AND WHY. The d-pad is the selector on the
title screen AND the walk in the game, and the game returns to the title
screen after GAME OVER - so a d-pad press that lands after the third lost
man moves `$0059` and the session's ramCheck stops naming the mountain it
selected. Measured: an idle body that presses nothing after START ends a
120 s run with `$0059` still at its own mountain, while a body that keeps
walking ends on the title screen with `$0059` at 31, 28 or 10 - wherever
its last presses left the number
(runs/f1417/iceclimber/probe/trace/*-synctrace.csv, watch:mountain). So
Popo's walking is in the ENTRY script, once, immediately after START, and
mountain-01-run.txt holds no direction at all. The walk block is one balanced
576-frame block, which is over inside the game on every mountain measured
and therefore cannot reach the title screen's number.
THE RAM CHECK, AND WHAT IT PROVES. Every value's ramCheck reads $0059 off
the session's final state and expects the mountain's own 0-based index
(MOUNTAIN 02 = 01 ... MOUNTAIN 32 = 1F). $0059 is Data Crystal's 'Ice
Climber (NES)/RAM map' entry '0x0059 Level Number - Starts at 0 for level
1. Updates at the start of every new level or when changing the level on
the start screen'
(https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Ice_Climber_(NES)/RAM_map, read through
the Wayback Machine: the live page is behind a JS challenge). It is a
CONSEQUENCE byte: no session pins anything, so the game wrote it, and the
check says 'this session's own selection is still the number the game
holds at the end' - which is exactly what a session that never took the
select cannot say. Its one structural limit is stated rather than hidden:
because the title screen is also where the selector lives, the check holds
only as long as nothing moves the number while the title is up, which is
what the entry/body split above buys.
AND THE GAME ITSELF MOVES IT. The title screen keeps the session's own
selection, but its attract demo - once the title has been up long enough -
starts a game of its own at MOUNTAIN 01 and writes 00 into $0059. Measured
on the sweep's own 31 sessions, 2026-09-26: 25 read their own index and 6
read 00 (MOUNTAIN 03, 10, 11, 12, 23, 24), which are the six whose GAME
OVER came early enough for the demo to begin inside the 120 s. The trace
is runs/f1417/iceclimber/probe/trace/t03/rec-synctrace.csv: GAME OVER at
frame 3 903, the title up and $0059 still 02, and at frame 6 903 $0059
reading 00 with lives back at 3. mountain-32 reaches GAME OVER at frame
4 803 and its demo never begins, so it reads 1F throughout. So a 00 here
is 'the tail of this session is the title screen and the demo' and not
'the session never warped': ADR-0239 s4's gate is the new count, and all
31 sessions pass it. This is the shape the Punch-Out!! profile records for
its $0001 - 'the byte is right and the instant was wrong' - and the shape
Excitebike's records under 'a failing check is not always a broken run'.
runs/f1417/iceclimber/RESULT.md carries the per-session table.
WHAT THE SELECTOR DOES NOT REACH, and what this sweep therefore does not
hold. Each mountain is eight floors and then a bonus round (booklet: 'The
screen is cleared after you arrive at the 8th floor, and you go into the
bonus round.', with ten vegetable types and the first bonus round always
eggplants), and the 120 s body is blind: it dies its way through the three
men in about 45 s and the rest of the run is the title screen. So a
session's pack holds the mountain's opening screen - the zoomed-out view
of the whole mountain with the condor carrying the vegetable, and the first
floor or two of play - and not the floors above, not the bonus round, and
not the mountain-clear transition. Those are ADR-0239 s1 rung 3 work (search
or chain per room) that a later measurement has to name, and the mid-run
geography is measured per session in runs/f1417/iceclimber/RESULT.md off
the scroll counters the same RAM map publishes: 0x008A, 0x008D and 0x0090
'Number of screen scrolls upwards'.
THE STAGE-CLEAR TRANSITION IS NEVER RECORDED, and the entry/body split
does not change that: a session starts at the mountain it selected and the
game's own level advance is not part of the 120 s. The union metric of
ADR-0239 s5 makes that invisible, so it is written here and in RESULT.md.
NO LIVES PIN. ADR-0239 s3 permits a lives pin to ride with a navigation
pass when the profile's inert control passes byte-identically, and the
control was run: see the _inertnessComment below. It failed, so this
profile carries no pin and no process in this sweep is launched with a
cheat at all.
_inertnessComment: ADR-0239 s3's inert control, measured on this binary, 2026-09-26, over the
same input script the sweep uses and the same 120 s budget, comparing the
whole textures/ tree with diff -rq and the two final states with
scripts/mss_ram.py --diff. Both arms are under
runs/f1417/iceclimber/probe/lives/ (unversioned).
$0020 is Data Crystal's '0x0020 Lives Remaining'
(https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Ice_Climber_(NES)/RAM_map), and it is
the byte the game shows as the men in reserve. It reads 0 on the title
screen and 3 once START begins the game, so 3 is the counter's start
value and 0020:03 is the pin s3 names.
The control FAILS. Uncheated: 222 files under textures/, 61 of them
absent from the pinned tree and 135 differing. Pinned: 164 files, 3 of
them absent from the uncheated tree. 385 of the 2 048 internal-RAM bytes
differ between the two final states, and the pinned run plays materially
longer (its $008D reads 1 against the uncheated run's 0). That is the
expected direction - the cheat substitutes the byte on the CPU read bus
(CheatManager::ApplyCheat), so the game reads 3 every time it looks and
the count-out never arrives. s3's condition is a byte-identical tree, so
the pin is refused. The same table, with the exact commands, is in
runs/f1417/iceclimber/RESULT.md.
So the blind body is allowed to lose its three men and to reach GAME
OVER, which is what ADR-0184 s4 asks for. Deaths and respawns are in
every session.
_provenanceComment: romSha1 is the No-Intro SHA1 of the user's own library dump, the one every
entry script and every ramCheck of this profile was measured against
NROM - 1 PRG bank, 1 CHR bank, mapper 0). It is the hash
scripts/stages/iceclimber/stage-set.json declares. The ROM is never copied

navigation.label: the title menu's MOUNTAIN row (MOUNTAIN 01-32), walked with the d-pad and begun with START
navigation.source: Ice Climber instruction booklet (Nintendo of America, 1985), 'Rules and Suggestions' 1: 'Use the control pad when the game menu is displayed to enter the number of the mountain you want to climb. (MOUNTAIN XX)' and 'The mountains are numbered from 1 ~ 32. You can attempt to climb any mountain, but the larger the number the more difficult the mountain is to climb.'; the controller page for SELECT (the hammer mark) and START (begin). The entry scripts are generated by scripts/stages/iceclimber/mountain-entry.py, which carries the press-shape measurements. ADR-0239 s1 rung 1: input, no cheat.

_defaultsComment: entry is the route MOUNTAIN 01 takes - the title menu's own default, START
and nothing else - and it is the before side of ADR-0239 s5, recorded
separately under runs/f1417/iceclimber/before/ and folded in with
--baseline. No value above uses it: each names its own entry script,
because walking the selector is what selects the mountain.
body is the one script every session repeats (ADR-0239 s6). It holds no
d-pad direction, which is what keeps the title screen from moving the
number the ramCheck reads - see the note above, and mountain-entry.py.
seconds is ADR-0239 s6's 120 s budget.
